Research presents conflicting outcomes on whether cats truly understand human emotions. Several sources cite studies indicating cats can recognize human emotional cues like facial expressions, body language, and vocal tones, and respond with comforting behaviors [d1, d2, d3, d4]. For instance, cats have shown different brain responses to happy versus angry human faces [d5]. However, other expert opinions argue cats are too independent or that there is no scientific evidence they can read human thoughts or emotions, highlighting the ongoing debate in feline cognition research [d5].
